reading.title: Reading a simple map key
reading.text: Mona takes a map to an information desk. The compass rose shows directions. Latitude helps describe north or south position. The boundary marks the edge of the area. A satellite helps the GPS system find a position. Mona asks what the symbols mean and reads the legend. She checks the scale before comparing distances. The map is a simplified guide, and the current route may need checking.

reading.title: Choosing a route and reading instruments
reading.text: Mona reads a walking-route note. A telescope is on the viewing platform. The vehicle's odometer records distance traveled. The path leads toward the visitor center. A detour changes the usual route today. A waypoint marks a reference place along the route. Mona checks the note's date and asks staff about the change. She does not treat an old route image as proof that the path is open.

reading.title: Clarifying a navigation-app task
reading.text: Mona opens a navigation app before she walks. She reads the directions and checks the route. Traffic may affect the estimated time. If the route changes, the app may reroute the journey. Mona can share location with a chosen contact, but she checks whom she is sending it to. She looks at the screen while stopped. A map view may be old and does not guarantee current access.
